item.subject: science
item.stem:
Priya fills a plastic syringe with air and closes its opening tightly with her finger. When she pushes the plunger in, the air inside is compressed into a smaller volume.

Why can the air in the closed syringe be compressed?

options.A: The air particles themselves shrink when the plunger is pushed.
options.B: The air particles are far apart with large spaces between them, so they can be forced closer together.
options.C: The air particles change into liquid particles when pushed together.
options.D: The air particles escape through the walls of the syringe.
